item.title: OpenAI Fires Three Safety Researchers Over Breach of Trust
item.description:
OpenAI Fires Three Safety Researchers Over Breach of Trust

OpenAI has stood firm on its decision to dismiss three AI safety researchers, saying the firings were due to a “significant breach of trust” and violations of policies on handling sensitive information.

🔍 Overview

  • OpenAI doubled down on the decision to fire the three researchers.
  • The company stressed the action was about a breach of trust, not the researchers’ safety concerns.
  • An internal investigation uncovered breaches “beyond what’s outlined in the letter,” but details were not released.

📄 Company Statement

  • In a post on X, OpenAI said Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni were dismissed for violating “clear policies on handling sensitive information.”
  • The lab insisted the decision was not about the trio speaking out about the company or their AI‑safety concerns.

📨 Researchers’ Response

  • The three researchers published an open letter urging OpenAI to be more transparent about the decision.
  • In the letter and social‑media posts they said they believed they were fired for raising safety concerns and had acted “in line with OpenAI’s mission and within the working norms of the time.”

🔐 Context

  • Staff concern over the safety of frontier systems has grown after several high‑profile breaches, including OpenAI’s hack of Hugging Face.
  • Many employees are now calling for companies to slow down development and improve safeguards for self‑improving systems.

📊 Why It Matters

  • The incident highlights tension between internal safety advocacy and corporate policy enforcement.
  • Transparency around internal investigations and policy breaches remains a focal point for the AI‑research community.

🗂️ Affected Researchers

Researcher Stated Reason for Dismissal
Jasmine Wang Violated clear policies on handling sensitive information
Tomek Korbak Violated clear policies on handling sensitive information
Mikita Balesni Violated clear policies on handling sensitive information

item.title: Global Survey Reveals Widespread Concern Over AI Job Loss and Inequality
item.description:
Global Survey Reveals Widespread Concern Over AI Job Loss and Inequality

A global survey conducted across 37 countries has gathered data on public sentiment regarding the impact of artificial intelligence on employment and daily life.

🔍 Overview

The survey questioned 42,151 people from February 8th to May 13th. Findings indicate a general trend of concern regarding the societal impacts of AI:

  • General Sentiment: A global median of 41 percent of respondents feel equally concerned and excited about AI, 37 percent are primarily concerned, and 13 percent are primarily excited.
  • Economic Impact: Respondents are generally more likely to say AI will increase the gap between rich and poor.
  • Employment: In 34 of the 37 countries surveyed, people believe AI is more likely to lead to job losses over the next 20 years than to create new jobs.

⚙️ Key details

Concerns regarding AI vary by region and age demographic:

Region/Demographic Detail
Australia 76 percent worry about AI impact
South Korea 76 percent worry about AI impact
United States 71 percent worry about AI impact
Older people More likely to be concerned about AI’s impact on daily life than younger people
Younger adults (18–34) Most likely to have mixed feelings about how AI will shape the world

Additionally, concern among younger demographics has risen sharply over the past year in the US, Sweden, Poland, Japan, Australia, and Brazil. In the US and Sweden, these younger groups are now as worried about AI-driven inequality and job loss as older generations.

💡 Why it matters

These public concerns align with warnings from industry leaders, such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who warned that AI could eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs.

#AI #Employment #PublicOpinion #Economy

Source: AI is feared globally as the destroyer of jobs
